Mr. Md. Meshbahul Islam Asif, Advocate, Fen the Petitioners. 
None appears, For the opposite party.
parties:
MD. GOLAM NABI BEING DEAD HIS LEGAL HEIRS: 1(A) MD. NURUL ISLAM AND OTHERS 
V. 
MD. SHAMSUZZOHA
full_judgment:
Md. Mozibur Rahman Miah J: At the instance of the predecessor of the present-petitioner nos. 1(a)-1(i), Md. Golam Nabi, the defendant in Title Suit No. 219 of 2007, this rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the Judgment and decree dated 02.07.2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Meherpur in Title Appeal No. 61 of 2010 dismissing the appeal and affirming the Judgment and decree dated 18.02.2010 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Meherpur in Title Suit No. 219 of 2007 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The relevant facts for the purpose of disposal of the instant rule are:

3. The present-opposite party as plaintiff filed the aforesaid suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit properties measuring an area of 7 decimals of land. The case as has been set-out in this revisional application in short is that, that the suit properties of the disputed khatian originally belonged to one, Ram Mohini Dashi and others and at the request of the Muslim Community of Biddadhorpur village to the said Jomindar to donate 7 decimals of land for erecting a mosque, he then gave 7 decimals of land for use as mosque. But without erecting any mosque, the local people took a decision that the mosque will be created not in the suit property but at the adjacent land. However, in the S.A record, the suit land was wrongly prepared in the name of the father of the defendant, Yead Ali in collusion with the survey official, but in the possession column, the said land was mentioned as mosque and ditch possessed by the local Muslim people subsequently, for the permanent earning source to maintain the said mosque, it was decided by the member of mosque committee to build some shop over the said 7 decimals of land. There had been a youth club adjacent west to the suit plot being No. 4026 for an area of 4 decimals of land and upon adding that 4 decimals of land with 7 decimals of land the local people used to enjoy title and possession over the same. While R.S. record was going on, the local people then made a query at the survey office when they came to learn that R.S khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant in R.S plot No. 496 appertaining to R.S khatian No. 105. It has further been stated that, the defendant had no title and possession over the suit property rather the local people have been enjoying the same for long 62-65 years. However, the S.A and R.S record was wrongly prepared in the name of the defendant and hence the plaintiff filed the suit.

4. On the contrary, the predecessor of the present-petitioner as defendant no. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending that, the father of the defendant named, Yead Ali took settlement of 7 decimals of land of the suit plot no. 427 and that of 2 decimals of land of plot no. 314 on 13 জ্যৈষ্ঠ, 1359BS by way of settlement (fordi) and accordingly in R.S khatian no. 165 as well as S.A khatian, the said 7 decimals of land has correctly been prepared in his name through in the comment column, it has wrongly been mentioned to be possessed by the local people as of "mosque". It has further been stated that, the property had not been purchased by the member of mosque committee and this defendant by filling earth over the said property erected some shops and by renting out the same he has been leading his life and finally prays for dismissal of the suit.

5. In order to dispose of the suit, the learned Assistant Judge framed as many as 5 different issues and both the plaintiff and the defendant adduced several witness and also produced documents in support of their respective cases. However, the learned Assistant Judge, on conclusion of the trial, finally dismissed the suit on contest against the defendant No. 1. But in the said Judgment the trial court came to a decision that, the defendant could not prove its acquiring title in the suit properties that is, in 7 decimals of land by virtue of the settlement (lordly) alleged to have executed on 13 জ্যৈষ্ঠ, 1359 BS in favour of the predecessor of the defendant, Yead Ali by the Jomindar.

6. However, challenging the said Judgment and decree of dismissal the plaintiff did not prefer any appeal but the defendant being aggrieved with the said observation denying his title of acquiring suit property preferred a title appeal being Title Appeal No. 61 of 2010 before the learned District Judge, Meherpur.

7. The said appeal was on transfer heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Meherpur. It is to be mentioned here that, during pendency of the appeal, the defendant filed three separate applications namely, an application under Order 6 Rule 17, application under Order 41 Rule 23 and that of an application under Order 41 Rule 27(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

8. However, the learned Joint District Judge, by rejecting all those 3 applications eventually dismissed the appeal and thereby affirmed the Judgment and decree passed by the trial court who dismissed the suit.

9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said Judgment, the predecessor of the present-petitioners as defendant filed the revisional application and obtained the instant rule.

10. It is worthwhile to mention hear that, the plaintiff had neither preferred appeal before the appellate court below nor filed any revision challenging the Judgment and order passed by the appellate court below rather the defendant preferred the appeal as well as filed this revisional application.

11. Mr. Md. Meshbahul Islam Asif, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner upon taking me to the revisional application and other material and evidence on record and that of the application so have been annexed as of Annexure-A series at the very outset submits that, the defendant-petitioner just disagreeing with the observation made by the trial court denying the acquiring of title by the predecessor of the defendant in the suit property preferred the appeal and that of the instant revision.

12. The learned counsel goes on to submit that, in the memo of appeal the defendant as appellant in its paragraph no. 5, 6 and 11 very candidly contends that, in support of acquiring title over the suit property that is, the settlement porcha through had been produced is the trial court and it had also taken into consideration by the trial court on 03.07.2000 but inadvertently the said document was not marked as exhibit.

13. It has further been contended that, since the document was produced before the trial court so under the provision of Order 27 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the appellate court below could have easily taken the said document as of additional evidence and sent back the ease on remand to the trial court to consider the said document as the appellate court is always considered to be the continuation of the trial court under the provision of section 107(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

<u>14. By refuting the observation made by the trial court that no document has been produced in support of acquiring title by the defendant in the suit property and the appellate court below though given a very exhaustive Judgment but did not take into consideration of the document so placed before it and that very non-consideration of those material documents was clearly stated in the memo of appeal but without considering the same, the appellate court below very misconceively dismissed the contention taken by the defendant-petitioner.</u>

15. The learned counsel further submits that, since the trial court while dismissed the suit has disbelieved the acquisition of title of the defendant in the observation meaning denying title of the defendant over the suit property, for which he preferred appeal where he assigned clear reasoning as to why the observation of the trial court is wrong but the appellate court below in its Judgment did not take into account of the said vital aspect and erroneously dismissed the appeal.

16. The learned counsel finally submits that, since the documents is available with the lower court records even this Hon'ble Court can go through the said record and came to a proper decision against the observation made by the trial court.

17. With such submission the learned counsel finally prays for expunging the observation made by the trial court in its Judgment.

18. I have considered the submission so advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the revisional application, the memo of appeal and have also gone through three applications so mentioned therein above at length.

19. During the course of hearing of this rule, the learned counsel also draws my attention to the settlement porcha (ফর্দি) dated জ্যৈষ্ঠ 1359BS through which the father of the defendant alleged to have acquired the suit property.

20. Moreover, after acquiring the suit property the defendant also paid rent and latest khatian also stands in its name so all those documentary evidence clearly demonstrates that, the defendants has acquired indefeasible title and possession over the suit property by virtue of the said settlement dated 13 জ্যৈষ্ঠ, 1359BS. But since the document had not been marked exhibit by the trial court though it was produced which can not be said to be any mistake on the part of the defendant-petitioner but by the trial court. Since the documents were lying with the record and I find the proposition advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner is correct, so I am of the view that, the Judgment passed by the appellate court below cannot sustain in law.

21. In the result, the rule is made absolute.

22. The judgment and decree so passed by the appellate court below dated 02.07.2013 is hereby set-aside.

23. Obviously, the observation so made by the trial court in its Judgment while disposing of issue nos. 1, 4 and 5 to the effect that:

বিবাদী পক্ষ দাবি করিয়াছে যে, নালিশী জমি বিবাদীর পিতা ইয়াদ আলী বাংলা ১৩৫৯ সালের ১৩ ই জৈষ্ঠ ফর্দিমুলে বন্দোবস্ত নিয়াছিলেন কিম্ত বিবাদী পক্ষ ফর্দি আদালতে প্রদর্শনী চিহ্তি করে নাই। ফলে নালিশী জিতে বিবাদীর কোন স্বত নাই।

24. Hence it is held that, the defendant-petitioners have title and possession over the suit property.

25. However, the operative portion of Judgment passed by the trial court dated 18.12.2010 is hereby maintained.

26. With the above, direction and observation, the rule is hereby made absolute.

27. Let a copy of this Judgment along with the lower court records be set to the court concern at once.

End.
